The FOMC statement strikes a cautiously constructive tone—solid job gains, moderate growth, subdued inflation with a symmetric 2% objective, and gradual policy normalization. Incorporating the July 2017 SLOOS slightly tempers that tone: banks reported weaker demand for CRE (including construction, land development, and multifamily) and for consumer credit (auto and cards), alongside tighter standards for consumer loans, while foreign banks tightened standards on C&I and CRE. These point to modest headwinds for credit growth and investment, partially offset by easing in several mortgage categories (jumbo/QM/GSE) and broadly unchanged standards for home-purchase and HELOCs. Net effect: still mildly positive, but closer to neutral than the initial read.
